metadata.description: ONE class for every execution (maintainer ruling 2026-08-04): a Job is the tracked, inspectable record of running something — the receipt of consuming a definition. Jobs are how an execution is started (submit intent for a Job) and stopped (a change request against it); a run's lifecycle rides the D7 execution_state axis, one Job per run (concurrency honest). No per-domain subtypes: the bound definition carries the schemas (its inputs_schema validates parameters, its outputs_schema validates results), so domain filtering is a DERIVED facet of the reference, queried not typed (job.running?family=automation — the ADR-038 §10 filtering surface). Instantiable base ("Base Classes are instantiable" — portability at its highest level); types appear later only if a genuinely job-shaped variant earns one. Every state transition seals with its pathway_ref; current state + results live on the record (act-now), history in the ledger (ADR-059 claims discipline). This is the udlm#330 start/stop model — an operation is a governed Job, not a bespoke verb surface.

definition_ref.description: The versioned definition artifact this job executes — the playbook, workflow, pipeline, or script the engine runs. Always a typed reference, never an inline body or a provider-native id: either a resource Reference (common-elements §2.5) to the entity carrying the definition, or a data_reference (DCM ADR-012) pinning an immutable automation_definition reference-data layer version — the pin that lets each promotion stage run exactly the definition version it verified, and lets rehydration replay the intent together with its payload. Optional: a job discovered on a brownfield engine may not yet cite its definition. Either form of URF reference is legal: a resource reference (estate/<handle>) to the entity carrying the definition, or a data reference (uuid/<v4>?reference_data_type==<kind>) pinning an immutable reference-data revision — the URL says which, and check_data_references enforces the kind on the data-reference form.

parameters.description: Parameters the definition is invoked with — the org-authored automation intent (a patch policy, a reboot policy, maintenance windows) that must survive an engine migration byte-identical. Keys are defined by the referenced definition; the substrate carries them opaquely and the provider validates them against the pinned definition at naturalization (T9 — the substrate never translates them into a provider-native spec).

targets.description: The resources this job operates on — typed resource references — URF strings (identifier-scheme §9), never inventory strings. Each is authored by handle (ADR-025 §2 — a uuid is never hand-authored; the control plane resolves it to the uuid form at reserve). Part of the portable automation intent: the target set is engine-neutral and unchanged by an engine migration. Distinct from the informational affected_entities edge: targets is authored intent (what the job is FOR); affected_entities records what a run actually touched.

max_execution_time.description: ISO 8601 duration (e.g. PT30M). MANDATORY per ENT-004; enforced by the substrate Lifecycle Constraint Enforcer.

on_max_exceeded.description: Action when max_execution_time is exceeded. Default is profile-governed (ENT-004).

trigger.description: What initiates the job (e.g. a NUT on-battery event, a cron schedule, an operator).

schedule.description: Scheduled-execution intent — meaningful only when trigger is 'schedule'. Carries the data the trigger enum value alone cannot: when the job runs, what happens when a run would overlap a still-running predecessor, and what happens to a missed window.

expression.description: Schedule expression, cron syntax (adopted vocabulary: Kubernetes CronJob .spec.schedule). The provider naturalizes it to its native scheduler.

overlap_policy.description: What happens when a scheduled run fires while the previous run is still executing (CronJob concurrencyPolicy cross-walk): allow concurrent runs, forbid the new run, or replace (supersede) the running one.

missed_run_policy.description: What happens to a run whose window was missed (engine down, job suspended): skip it, or catch_up — run once as soon as possible (CronJob startingDeadlineSeconds semantics).

results.description: The run's results, shaped by the bound definition's outputs_schema — what dependent steps and readiness gates read. Current-state data (act-now); per-transition history is the ledger's.

started_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant execution entered EXECUTING.

completed_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC instant execution reached COMPLETED/FAILED/CANCELLED.

relationships.name: executes_definition
relationships.description: Consumer-declared — the Job declares what it executes: exactly one definition, today an Automation.* class member (the target widens if a second family-Process category of definitions ever exists). The domain facet (family/category filters) derives from this edge.

relationships.name: executor_host
relationships.description: Executor host(s) — where the job runs. A running job pins its executor: in a reverse-topological lifecycle operation the executor cannot stop until the job completes ('orchestrator stops last', derived, not special-cased).

relationships.name: fabric
relationships.description: Fabric the job traverses to reach its targets — connectivity outlives whatever the job is operating on.

relationships.name: resolver
relationships.description: Name/address resolution the job uses to reach targets (typically soft — inventories can pin IPs).

affected_entities (§6.3) — entities this job creates/modifies/decommissions. Informational; §6.4 makes the provenance obligation flow the OTHER way (affected entity cites the job uuid). NOTE: the declared target is representative — affected entities may be of ANY resource type; this edge is informational and never constrains what a job may touch (the former bare 'Compute' category target was not a registered type).

adopts.role: run-to-completion and scheduled-job vocabulary (activeDeadlineSeconds ≈ max_execution_time, terminal states; CronJob schedule/concurrencyPolicy/startingDeadlineSeconds ≈ schedule.expression/overlap_policy/missed_run_policy)

context.purpose: The source of truth for executions — start, stop, track, and inspect a run of anything as one governed object, with results readable and every transition sealed.
context.plain_description: A Job is one run. Starting something means submitting intent for a Job bound to a definition; stopping it is a change request against the Job; inspecting it is reading the record (current execution state, results) and walking its seals (who started it, why, what each transition was). Discovery runs, automation runs, and operational actions (power on a host) are all Jobs — one lifecycle, one retention family, one query surface.
use_when: You start or stop an execution of anything — the governed alternative to a bespoke verb API (udlm#330)
You need what's-running-now against a resource (blast radius gains the mid-flight dimension as a plain query)
You need a run's results as readable state for dependent steps or readiness gates
not_for: The definition of WHAT can run (Automation.* classes — offered, not executed)
Run HISTORY beyond current state (the ledger's — a Job record makes state claims only)
works_with: Automation.OSPatch.EngineBlue / EngineGreen — the engines a provider realizes the run through
